newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Turkmens to hold C Asian summit on energy.
newsitem.headline: Turkmens to hold C Asian summit on energy.

text.p: Turkmenistan will host a regional summit on May 13-14 to discuss ways to export the land-locked area's oil and gas riches, the former Soviet republic's official Turkmen-Press news agency said on Monday.

Leaders of Iran, Turkey, Pakistan, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and unnamed respresentatives from Afghanistan are expected to attend the meeting of the Economic Cooperation Organisation in the capital Ashgabat, the agency said.
It said the participants plan to sign a set of accords over regional transport and communications.
"Urgent priority will be paid in the declaration to the construction of oil and gas pipelines," the agency said.
The former Soviet republics surrounding the Caspian Sea are sitting on huge reserves of oil and gas but remain almost totally reliant on Moscow for limited use of Russia's pipeline network.

The war in Afghanistan is also likely to figure in discussions. Central Asian leaders fear a spring advance northwards by the fundamentalist Islamic Taleban militia, who want to take control of northern provinces bordering the ex-Soviet states.
